clue.text: One's fretted over time, Cautious Craig in bits

indicators.note: something in bits has been broken up, so the letters are scattered and reassembled

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A careful man called Craig falls to pieces after fretting for ages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fretted' looks like worried, but here it means fitted with frets, the ridges on a guitar's neck.
explanation.definitionFit: An acoustic guitar is an instrument whose neck carries frets, so it is one thing that is literally fretted.

clue.text: Skilled champ sliced shot taking on hole

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
a hole is round, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A skilled golf champion slices a shot while playing a hole.
explanation.walkthrough: The golf words sliced, shot and hole all pose as one scene; 'sliced' is fodder and 'shot' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Accomplished describes someone highly trained and expert, a direct synonym of skilled.

clue.text: Over bog, backside of addict gets injected many times

indicators.note: the backside of a word is its rear end, so only its final letter is kept
an injection goes inside, so this letter is put into the middle of the others

blocks.note: O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
a fen is marshy, boggy land
the last letter of addict

explanation.surface: Sitting on the toilet, a drug user keeps shooting up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bog' is British slang for a toilet, which drives the surface, but the wordplay wants a marsh.
explanation.definitionFit: Often means frequently, on numerous occasions, which is what many times expresses.

clue.text: Small footwear: they might be hurting

blocks.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
trainers is the British word for sneakers

explanation.surface: Shoes a size too small will leave your feet sore.
explanation.definitionFit: People straining their muscles or efforts are putting themselves through pain, so strainers may well be hurting.

clue.text: Cool cheese at front of fridge quickly

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening, so only the first letter is used

blocks.note: in means fashionable, cool
Brie is a soft French cheese
the first letter of fridge

explanation.surface: Chilled cheese is kept at the front of the fridge for a quick snack.
explanation.definitionFit: In brief means briefly or in a few words, so said quickly without lingering.

clue.text: Put on tie, not wanting, ultimately to go out

indicators.note: ultimately points to the end, so only the final letter of the word before it is kept
going out suggests leaving the proper order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the last letter of wanting

explanation.surface: Someone dressing for an evening out decides they don't want a tie.
explanation.definitionFit: To get into clothes is to dress oneself in them, the same as putting them on.

clue.text: Victor spilling wife's secret

indicators.note: spilling something means letting it fall out, so that letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: a victor is the winner
W is the standard abbreviation for wife

explanation.surface: The champion blurts out his wife's secret.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are private ones, kept hidden within, which is what secret means here.

clue.text: Forever restricting grassland for walks

indicators.note: restricting something means hemming it in, so one word is held inside the other

blocks.note: always means forever
a ley is a field temporarily sown with grass

explanation.surface: Fencing off meadows permanently so people can take walks.
explanation.walkthrough: A ley is a British farming word for land put down to grass for a few years.
explanation.definitionFit: Alleyways are narrow passages used on foot, so they are walks in the sense of paths.

clue.text: Supply food in college diner without starter

indicators.note: a starter is what comes first, so the opening letter is removed

blocks.note: C is an abbreviation for college
a diner is someone who eats

explanation.surface: A college canteen serves meals but skips the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starter' plays on the first course of a meal, but it means the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To cater is to provide meals and refreshments, as a caterer does for an event.

clue.text: Attracted to men or women tickling in a way that's cruel

blocks.note: short for bisexual
a tickling feeling is a tingly one

explanation.surface: A flirt teases both sexes in a way that turns out to be heartless.
explanation.definitionFit: Bitingly describes remarks that are sharp and wounding, so done cruelly.

clue.text: DJ is one equalizing deck

blocks.note: evening things up means making them equal
to deck is to adorn or dress

explanation.surface: A disc jockey levels the sound on the turntable deck.
explanation.walkthrough: DJ looks like a disc jockey, which makes 'deck' feel like a turntable; here DJ is a dinner jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A dinner jacket is formal wear for night-time occasions, an example of the category of formal clothing.

clue.text: One's naked, essentially wearing short, revealing piece

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept
whoever is wearing a garment is inside it, so these letters go within the next word

blocks.note: an is the indefinite article, meaning one
the middle letter of naked
mini means short, as in a miniskirt

explanation.surface: Someone nearly nude wears only a tiny skimpy item.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for has, joining the first two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A mankini is a skimpy men's one-piece swimsuit that leaves almost all the body on show.

clue.text: Go back and watch the fifth dancer

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the word is read in reverse

blocks.note: to run is to go
to eye something is to watch it
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Rewind and see the fifth performer again.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Nureyev was a famous Russian ballet star, so he is an example of a dancer.

clue.text: Failing courses with English

blocks.note: laps are circuits of a course
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A student is failing their courses, including English.
explanation.definitionFit: A lapse is a slip or a moment of failure, such as a lapse in judgment.

clue.text: Stay with a swinger, maybe and reproduce

blocks.note: a stay is a support, a prop
taken as written
a gate swings on its hinges

explanation.surface: Spend the night with a partner-swapper and start a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swinger' suggests a partner-swapper, but 'maybe' flags an example: a gate swings.
explanation.definitionFit: To propagate is to breed or multiply, especially plants or animals, so to reproduce.

clue.text: McDonald's to take one order for consumers, naturally?

blocks.note: first meaning: a business with many fast-food outlets
second meaning: in ecology, the sequence in which living things eat one another

explanation.surface: A fast-food counter taking a single customer's order.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order' and 'consumers' sound like restaurant talk, but 'naturally' moves them into biology.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both a restaurant franchise and the ecological ranking of predators and prey.

clue.text: Soccer ground hosting final getting louder and louder

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed up, so the letters are rearranged
a host takes in a guest, so one set of letters holds the other

blocks.note: taken as written
the end is the final part

explanation.surface: A football stadium staging the cup final grows noisier as the match goes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soccer ground' reads as a stadium; 'ground' is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual increase in volume, a musical term for sound building up.

clue.text: Plants bordering new gardens? These might come out for purchase in winter?

definitions.text: These might come out for purchase in winter

indicators.note: a border runs around the edge, so these letters surround the next one

blocks.note: to plant seeds is to sow them
N is the abbreviation for new
to hoe is to work the garden

explanation.surface: Shoppers buy winter bedding plants and garden gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Purchase' looks like buying, but it means grip on a slippery surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Snowshoes are frames strapped to boots that give walkers grip and support on deep snow.

clue.text: Concerned with Royal Mail covering area for delivery?

blocks.note: to argue over something is to be concerned with it
A is the abbreviation for area
the initials of the British postal service

explanation.surface: The postal service serving a district to deliver letters.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Mail and delivery suggest the post, but delivery is bowling in cricket. The setter lets the postal initials sit after the area letter here.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a ball is delivered by the bowler, and bowling with the arm above the shoulder is the overarm method.

clue.text: Security on the borders checks procedures

indicators.note: the borders of a word are its edges, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: the outer letters of security
to stem a flow is to check it

explanation.surface: Border security runs checks according to set procedures.
explanation.definitionFit: Systems are organised methods of doing things, the same as established procedures.

clue.text: Stain one's pants touring India

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so these letters are badly made and must be reworked
touring means going around, so these letters wrap around another

blocks.note: taken as written, ignoring the apostrophe
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A traveller in India finds a mark on their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants in Britain means underpants, which the surface uses, and also means rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Eosin is a red dye used in laboratories to colour tissue samples, so it is a stain.

clue.text: Paper exercise around large case study

indicators.note: around means on all sides, so these letters enclose the next one

blocks.note: an exam paper
physical education
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A test paper built around one big case study.
explanation.definitionFit: An example is a single instance taken to illustrate a point, much as a case study is.

clue.text: Conspiracy surrounding international leader

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing on every side, so one word goes around the other

blocks.note: a plot is a conspiracy
I is the abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: A scheme closing in on a world leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot guides a ship or aircraft, and a pilot scheme leads the way, so it serves as a guide or leader.

clue.text: Disgusted to live with duke – where one lies, poorly?

blocks.note: sick of something means disgusted by it
to be is to exist, to live
D is the abbreviation for duke; 'with' just adds it on

explanation.surface: Someone revolted at having to share a home with an aristocrat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' looks like an adverb about lying badly, but it is the British word for ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A sickbed is the bed of someone unwell, where an ill person stays lying down.

clue.text: I love British flipping pancakes

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the letters are read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: taken as written
love is a score of zero in tennis
B is the abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: Someone declares their passion for tossing pancakes on Pancake Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' suits pancakes perfectly, so it feels part of the picture; it is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Blini are small Russian buckwheat pancakes, often served with caviar and sour cream.

clue.text: Informal situation of party: up for it?

blocks.note: a ball is a formal dance party
game means willing, up for it

explanation.surface: Someone sizing up a casual party and asking whether you're keen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Informal' marks the definition as colloquial: a whole new ballgame is slang for a different situation.
explanation.definitionFit: In casual speech a ballgame is a state of affairs, as in the idiom a whole new ballgame.

clue.text: Turn on TV, mostly after current talk

indicators.note: turning something around makes it face the other way, so the word is read backwards
mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: taken as written
I is the physics symbol for electric current
a TV is a television set

explanation.surface: Switching the television on mainly for current-affairs chat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn on TV' reads as one instruction, but 'Turn' acts on 'on' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Noise can mean idle talk or rumours, as in making noises about something.

clue.text: Bit tired, some kids doze, ultimately getting off with these?

definitions.text: Bit tired, some kids doze, ultimately getting off with these?

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the last letter of each of the two words before it is kept
getting off suggests leaving the right place, so the letters are jumbled into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of kids
the last letter of doze

explanation.surface: Sleepy children drift off while being read to at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: a little tired, some children nod off listening to these.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedtime stories are tales read to children at night to help them settle and fall asleep.
